Windows Defender isn't very good. There are so many better alternatives that are also free.

Defender is actually quite good. However when IT Security Experts score it there is a bit of a handicap that it suffers.

These tests are always performed using the latest service pack with no other OS patches applied. This is a good base line as it affords the maximum number of items to base your test on.so you have a larger variation to quantify on what's a good security suite and what's bad.

Why this is a handicap for Windows Defender is there are certain attacks which are best left to an OS patch where as other attacks are best left to a middleware security suite. It doesn't make much sense for Microsoft to address the same attack twice; once in an OS patch, and again with Windows Defender. You could argue that doing this would be inefficient and bloat the program.

In my experience and research I'd put Windows Defender at #3 with Kepersky and Symantec at #1 and #2. The only reason why Defender rates lower than these two is that Keperskey and Symantec have a long track record of being first to deploy patches for current attacks. Microsoft for various reasons normally doesn't deploy updates until patch Tuesday unless there is a critical reason for it. Keperskey and Symantec have a much more fluid release schedule.

The people who need antivirus software the most are the people who haven't updated their computers recently. You can't (and shouldn't) rely on the OS being up when checking for security issues.

>You could argue that doing this would be inefficient and bloat the program.

The other software companies are able to find the viruses and other crap without the OS being up to date. Some of them do have bloated programs but others aren't. Microsoft is just being lazy.
